tagline: Nine beach towns along the route the mail once walked barefoot.
intro: A1A comes down from the Palm Beach County line at Deerfield Beach and runs about 32 miles through Pompano Beach, Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood to the Miami-Dade line, nine beach towns in all, alongside the Intracoastal Waterway and sea turtle nests on the beaches.

Before there was any road the mail walked. From 1885 to 1892 carriers went barefoot down the firm sand between Palm Beach and Miami, rowing where they had to, and in 1887 one of them, Ed Hamilton, never made it across Hillsboro Inlet. His clothes were found on the north bank.

moments.title: Hillsboro Inlet Light
moments.text: Turned down 17 times before it was lit in 1907, the light had a lens that, stopped at the wrong angle in the morning, focused the sun west and started fires in the Everglades.

moments.title: SS Copenhagen
moments.text: A British steamer carrying coal for Havana struck the reef off Lauderdale-by-the-Sea in 1900 and never came off, and it lies in 25 feet of water as an underwater archaeological preserve.

moments.title: Bonnet House
moments.text: Frederic Bartlett designed this Caribbean plantation-style winter house himself among dunes and mangroves, and of the monkeys his wife Evelyn bought to live in its trees, at least three remained in 2014.
